### Overview

In advanced sports analytics, play-by-play data provides the granular foundation needed to evaluate team efficiency, player performance, and tactical decisions. In this lab, we utilize **`nfl_data_py`**, a Python package that provides fast access to cleaned NFL play-by-play data embedded with advanced statistical metrics.

Starting with Play by Play (pbp) data

In the interest of speed, I've only taken regular season data from the first 4 weeks of the 2025 season.  
```{python}
# Fetch 2025 play-by-play data

raw_pbp_2025 = nfl.import_pbp_data([2025])

# Filter for Weeks 1-4 regular season scrimmage plays
pbp_w1_4 = raw_pbp_2025[
    (raw_pbp_2025['season_type'] == 'REG') &
    (raw_pbp_2025['week'] <= 4) &
    (raw_pbp_2025['posteam'].notna()) &
    (raw_pbp_2025['play_type'].isin(['pass', 'run']) | (raw_pbp_2025['pass'] == 1) | (raw_pbp_2025['rush'] == 1)) &
    (raw_pbp_2025['epa'].notna())
].copy()
```


```{python}

# Inspect dataset dimensions
print("Dataset dimensions (rows x cols):", pbp_w1_4.shape)
```

What variables are available to us:  
```{python}
list(pbp_w1_4.columns)
```

Only ~370 features/variables per play.  Let's take a look at the first 6 rows of these data:  

```{python}
pbp_w1_4.head(6)
```

The next set of code aggregates all of the play by play data by team. We get some variables based upon expected points added (EPA) per play. We do this aggregation by offense and defense then join them back together.  
```{python}
# Offensive Aggregation (posteam)
offense_summary = pbp_w1_4.groupby('posteam').apply(
    lambda x: pd.Series({
        'off_plays': len(x),
        'off_epa_per_play': x['epa'].mean(),
        'pass_epa': x.loc[x['pass'] == 1, 'epa'].mean(),
        'rush_epa': x.loc[x['rush'] == 1, 'epa'].mean(),
        'off_success_rate': x['success'].mean(),
        'dropback_pct': (x['pass'] == 1).mean()
    }),
    include_groups=False
).reset_index()

# Defensive Aggregation (defteam)
defense_summary = pbp_w1_4.groupby('defteam').apply(
    lambda x: pd.Series({
        'def_plays': len(x),
        'def_epa_allowed': x['epa'].mean(),
        'def_pass_epa_allowed': x.loc[x['pass'] == 1, 'epa'].mean(),
        'def_rush_epa_allowed': x.loc[x['rush'] == 1, 'epa'].mean(),
        'def_success_rate_allowed': x['success'].mean()
    }),
    include_groups=False
).reset_index()

# Join Offense & Defense into a single Master Team Summary
team_summary = pd.merge(
    offense_summary, 
    defense_summary, 
    left_on='posteam', 
    right_on='defteam'
).rename(columns={'posteam': 'team'}).drop(columns=['defteam'])

team_summary = team_summary.sort_values(by='off_epa_per_play', ascending=False)
```


```{python}
# Display top 5 teams by Offensive EPA
print("Top 5 Offensive Teams:")
print(team_summary.head(5).round(3).to_markdown(index=False))

# Display top 6 teams by Defensive EPA
team_summary = team_summary.sort_values(by='def_epa_allowed', ascending=True)
print("\nTop 6 Defensive Teams:")
print(team_summary.head(6).round(3).to_markdown(index=False))
```

##Drive summary data

So we are going back to the play by play data from 2025 and now we are going to look at some drive summaries.  



```{python}
pbp_clean = pbp_w1_4[
    (pbp_w1_4['drive'].notna()) &
    (pbp_w1_4['epa'].notna()) &
    (pbp_w1_4['play'] == 1) &
    (pbp_w1_4['play_type'].isin(['run', 'pass']))
].copy()
```

Next we group the data and since drives are numbered from the beginning of each game, we have to group by game and drive.  

```{python}
drive_level_data = pbp_clean.groupby(['game_id', 'drive', 'posteam', 'defteam']).agg(
    drive_total_epa=('epa', 'sum'),
    drive_mean_epa=('epa', 'mean'),
    play_count=('epa', 'count'),
    drive_result=('fixed_drive_result', 'first')
).reset_index()
```

Next take the drive level data and get some offensive and defensive summaries:  
```{python}
offense_drive_summary = drive_level_data[drive_level_data['posteam'].notna()].groupby('posteam').agg(
    drives=('drive_total_epa', 'count'),
    mean_drive_epa=('drive_total_epa', 'mean'),
    median_drive_epa=('drive_total_epa', 'median'),
    total_off_epa=('drive_total_epa', 'sum'),
    avg_plays_per_dr=('play_count', 'mean')
).reset_index().sort_values(by='mean_drive_epa', ascending=False)

print("Top 6 Offensive Drive Summaries:")
print(offense_drive_summary.head(6).round(3).to_markdown(index=False))

defense_drive_summary = drive_level_data[drive_level_data['defteam'].notna()].groupby('defteam').agg(
    drives_def=('drive_total_epa', 'count'),
    mean_epa_allowed=('drive_total_epa', 'mean'),
    median_epa_allow=('drive_total_epa', 'median'),
    total_def_epa=('drive_total_epa', 'sum'),
    avg_plays_allowed=('play_count', 'mean')
).reset_index().sort_values(by='mean_epa_allowed', ascending=True)

print("\nTop 6 Defensive Drive Summaries:")
print(defense_drive_summary.head(6).round(3).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## College Football Data
Below we do some practice with loading, summarizing and visualizing the college football data.  Using direct parquet imports from public repositories fetches pre-processed play-by-play data directly without requiring API key authentication. We aggregate play-level yardage to quantify offensive and defensive Yards Per Play (YPP) across the 2025 season.  

```{python}
# load the 2025 season
plays_df_polars = sdv.cfb.load_cfb_pbp(seasons=[2025], return_as_pandas=False)
games_df_polars = sdv.cfb.load_cfb_schedule(seasons=[2025], return_as_pandas=False)

# convert the polar files to pandas dataframe
pbp_2025_raw = plays_df_polars.to_pandas(use_pyarrow_extension_array=False)
games_df=games_df_polars.to_pandas(use_pyarrow_extension_array=False)
print("\n".join(games_df.columns))
# Filter down game metadata to isolate the home/away division tags
games_meta = games_df[['game_id', 'home_division', 'away_division','home_conference','away_conference']]

# 4. Merge the division tags onto your play-by-play data
final_pbp = pd.merge(pbp_2025_raw, games_meta, on='game_id', how='left')


```


```{python}
col_list = final_pbp.columns.tolist()
pd.set_option('display.max_seq_items', None)
print(col_list) 
print("\n".join(final_pbp.columns))
```




```{python}
# Filter for FBS vs FBS games and valid rushing/passing attempts
pbp_2025 = final_pbp[
    (final_pbp['home_division'] == 'fbs') & 
    (final_pbp['away_division'] == 'fbs') &
    ((final_pbp['rush'] == 1) | (final_pbp['pass'] == 1)) &
    (final_pbp['statYardage'].notna())
].copy()

pbp_2025 = pbp_2025.rename(columns={'statYardage': 'yards_gained'})

print(f"Dataset successfully loaded. Dimensions: {pbp_2025.shape}")
```



Note pbp for all college is a big file and includes teams from FBS, FCS, D2 and D3. We're only interested in FBS v FBS games today.  Below we get the yards per play gained for offenses.  
```{python}
# Compute offensive YPP by team
off_ypp = pbp_2025.groupby(['pos_team', ]).agg(
    off_plays=('yards_gained', 'count'),
    off_ypp=('yards_gained', 'mean')
).reset_index().rename(columns={'pos_team': 'team'}).sort_values(by='off_ypp', ascending=False)
```

# Let's look at who is best on this metric
```{python}
print(off_ypp.head(15).round(3).to_markdown(index=False))
```

Below we get the yards per play gained against defenses.  
```{python}
# Compute defensive YPP allowed by team
def_ypp = pbp_2025.groupby('def_pos_team').agg(
    def_plays=('yards_gained', 'count'),
    def_ypp=('yards_gained', 'mean')
).reset_index().rename(columns={'def_pos_team': 'team'}).sort_values(by='def_ypp', ascending=True)
```

```{python}
# Let's look at who is best

print(def_ypp.head(15).round(3).to_markdown(index=False))
```
Below we join and classify the teams into tiers.  
```{python}
# Join metrics and classify into performance tiers
all_ypp = pd.merge(off_ypp, def_ypp, on='team')

mean_off = all_ypp['off_ypp'].mean()
mean_def = all_ypp['def_ypp'].mean()

conditions = [
    (all_ypp['off_ypp'] > mean_off) & (all_ypp['def_ypp'] < mean_def),
    (all_ypp['off_ypp'] > mean_off) & (all_ypp['def_ypp'] >= mean_def),
    (all_ypp['off_ypp'] <= mean_off) & (all_ypp['def_ypp'] < mean_def)
]
choices = ["Elite", "High Offense / Low Defense", "Low Offense / High Defense"]
all_ypp['tier'] = np.select(conditions, choices, default="Rebuilding")

all_ypp['net_ypp'] = all_ypp['off_ypp'] - all_ypp['def_ypp']
all_ypp = all_ypp.sort_values(by='net_ypp', ascending=False)
```

Print out the data in a nice format.

```{python}
# Render structured output table
(
    GT(all_ypp[['team', 'off_ypp', 'def_ypp', 'net_ypp', 'tier']])
    .tab_header(
        title=md("**2025 FBS Yards Per Play Summary**"),
        subtitle="Evaluated on all rushing and passing attempts"
    )
    .cols_label(
        team="Team",
        off_ypp="Offensive YPP",
        def_ypp="Defensive YPP",
        net_ypp="Net YPP Margin",
        tier="Performance Tier"
    )
    .fmt_number(columns=["off_ypp", "def_ypp", "net_ypp"], decimals=2)
)
```

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from adjustText import adjust_text

# Set high-DPI theme and clean grid style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8), dpi=150)

# 1. Plot points with distinct borders and subtle transparency
sns.scatterplot(
    data=all_ypp, 
    x='off_ypp', 
    y='def_ypp', 
    hue='tier', 
    palette='Set1', 
    s=90,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5,
    alpha=0.85,
    ax=ax
)

# 2. Add quadrant reference lines
mean_off = all_ypp['off_ypp'].mean()
mean_def = all_ypp['def_ypp'].mean()

ax.axvline(mean_off, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
ax.axhline(mean_def, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)

# 3. Add team text labels with translucent background boxes
texts = []
for _, row in all_ypp.iterrows():
    t = ax.text(
        row['off_ypp'], 
        row['def_ypp'], 
        row['team'], 
        fontsize=8,
        fontweight='medium',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.6)
    )
    texts.append(t)

# Optimize label placement to prevent overlapping lines
adjust_text(
    texts, 
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color='gray', lw=0.4, alpha=0.6),
    expand=(1.2, 1.4),
    force_text=(0.2, 0.4)
)

# 4. Invert Y-axis (Lower defensive YPP allowed = better defense)
ax.invert_yaxis()

# 5. Add background quadrant annotations
xlim = ax.get_xlim()
ylim = ax.get_ylim()  # Note: ylim is inverted

ax.text(xlim[1], ylim[1], "GREAT OFFENSE\nGREAT DEFENSE  ", 
        ha='right', va='top', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color='green', alpha=0.35)
ax.text(xlim[0], ylim[0], "  POOR OFFENSE\n  POOR DEFENSE", 
        ha='left', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color='red', alpha=0.35)

# 6. Titles & Labels
ax.set_title("2025 Team Yards Per Play Matrix", fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.set_xlabel("Offensive YPP (Higher is Better)", fontsize=11, labelpad=8)
ax.set_ylabel("Defensive YPP Allowed (Lower is Better)", fontsize=11, labelpad=8)

# 7. Clean Legend
ax.legend(
    title="Performance Tier", 
    loc='upper center', 
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.1), 
    ncol=4, 
    frameon=True, 
    facecolor='white', 
    edgecolor='none'
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Get wins for each team in 2025

```{python}
if 'games_raw' in locals():
    # Calculate regular season wins per team
    home_wins = games_raw[games_raw['homePoints'] > games_raw['awayPoints']].groupby('homeTeam').size().reset_index(name='wins').rename(columns={'homeTeam': 'team'})
    away_wins = games_raw[games_raw['awayPoints'] > games_raw['homePoints']].groupby('awayTeam').size().reset_index(name='wins').rename(columns={'awayTeam': 'team'})

    total_wins = pd.concat([home_wins, away_wins]).groupby('team')['wins'].sum().reset_index()
```

```{python}
if 'talent_raw' in locals() and 'total_wins' in locals():
    # Clean talent scores, join wins, and extract regression residuals
    df_analytics = pd.merge(talent_raw[['team', 'talent']], total_wins, on='team').dropna()
    df_analytics['talent_score'] = df_analytics['talent'].astype(float)
```

```{python}
if 'df_analytics' in locals():
    # Fit OLS model to derive expected wins and residual performance
    model = smf.ols('wins ~ talent_score', data=df_analytics).fit()

    df_analytics['expected_wins'] = model.predict(df_analytics)
    df_analytics['win_residual'] = df_analytics['wins'] - df_analytics['expected_wins']
    df_analytics['efficiency'] = np.where(df_analytics['win_residual'] >= 0, "Overperforming", "Underperforming")
    df_analytics = df_analytics.sort_values(by='win_residual', ascending=False)

    # Tabulate top 5 overperforming teams relative to talent
    (
        GT(df_analytics[['team', 'talent_score', 'wins', 'expected_wins', 'win_residual', 'efficiency']].head(5))
        .tab_header(
            title=md("**Top 5 Talent Overperformers (2025)**"),
            subtitle="Teams exceeding expected win totals based on 247Sports Composite Talent"
        )
        .cols_label(
            team="Team",
            talent_score="Talent Score",
            wins="Actual Wins",
            expected_wins="Expected Wins",
            win_residual="Win Surplus",
            efficiency="Status"
        )
        .fmt_number(columns=["talent_score", "expected_wins", "win_residual"], decimals=2)
    )
```
